initialisation_reference.superseded_first_scoring: 640 windows under the pre-fix evaluator, kept as evaluation/init_step1_superseded_old_eval and ignored by the summariser
initialisation_reference.why_not_the_published_weights: the published pi05_libero checkpoint stores unmerged weights; restoring them into this round LoRA-shaped TrainState fails with a structure mismatch over lora_a/lora_b, so the initialisation reference is the earliest state this exact configuration can save: one optimizer step after loading the published weights

learning_rate_trace.claim: configuration trace; the trainer does not log the learning rate, so this is the value the registered schedule produces at each step
learning_rate_trace.source: openpi.training.optimizer.CosineDecaySchedule evaluated in the training image, with the schedule object the trainer itself builds

learning_rate_trace_note: not carried over: the previous record had no such field
rebuilt_from: config_initial.json, resource_registry.json, launcher logs, the evaluation driver manifest and every evaluation report.json

resource_ownership.cleanup_policy: exact registered entry plus confirm token; no broad filter, no purge, no daemon restart, no container that was not registered here
resource_ownership.identity_note: exact container id, name, owner and GPU UUID remain only in the ignored private registry

run.config_snapshot_gap: config_initial.json does not carry data_loader_workers or seed, so both are read from the registered container argv; the snapshot writer should record them for later rounds
run.norm_stats_binding: the run config names the train-only statistics by file hash and the frozen view binds them canonically; both are recorded so the same document is identified either way

record.source: run_initial.json written by the registered launcher on exit
record.timestamp_note: run_initial.json writes the same timestamp into both fields; wall_time_s is the measured duration and is authoritative

seed.applied_by: the sampler call in scripts/so101/train_so101.py passes this value as a literal, which is how the two stay equal; the run config snapshot does not carry it

step_mapping_note: the Orbax directory index is a zero-based loop index and TrainState.step is the applied-update counter, so directory d holds step d+1; this run therefore saves its intermediate checkpoints one update after each multiple of 5,000 while the final save still carries the targeted update count. Measured on this store, not assumed.

throughput_samples.outcome: replaced: container carried the pre-amendment 28800 s wall limit

throughput_samples.note: measured after the loader change; 30000 updates therefore need 8.78 h

training_split_openloop_curve.claim: train-split open-loop action prediction on recorded expert observations; not a closed-loop result

wall_limit.amendment: measured steady throughput on the registered card is 1.054 s per optimizer update (540 updates in 569 s at step 2752), so 30,000 updates need 8.78 h and cannot finish inside the pre-registered 8 h wall limit
